doc.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996

title: The Lunceford band as a show and dance band
summary: Shearing never heard Lunceford in person; Williams describes the band's showmanship, dance music, Willie Smith and 'Prelude No. 7'; Shearing recalls dancing to Sy Oliver playing Lunceford charts.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Unfortunately I never got over here in time to hear the Lunceford band.
Oh, man, well I can tell you anybody who did can tell you what an experience that was. They would swing you into bad health.
Great show band too, weren’t they?
When they’d play those shout things they’d all the front line stand up and — a great show band.

Oh, man, they would play the music for people like the Miller Brothers and Lois, and what is that, the tap dancing teams, and for ballroom danc--. They played everything absolutely elegant. What was that thing they played [scats].
Willie Smith and that whole bunch. But they could swing you into — I mean dance you to death. When they would start playing “River St. Marie” and they’d change keys, they’d say [scats]. Oh man.

Ellie and I talk all the time about the time that we went to Rockefeller Center for New Year’s and danced to Sy Oliver. And I said, “Can you give me a Lunceford?” First of all he played several Lunceford charts. I said, “Ellie, this is as close as you’re going to get.” But oh, that band.
They would dance us to death when they’d come to Chicago, you know? Every number. And the ballads were just as pretty.
